definitions.explanation: Describes something so minor or unimportant that it does not merit attention or discussion. Literally 'not sufficient to take up.'

examples.japanese: {取|と}るに{足|た}らない{問題|もんだい}だ。
そんな{取|と}るに{足|た}らないことで{悩|なや}むな。
examples.english: Don't worry about something so insignificant.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{取|と}るに{足|た}らない{人物|じんぶつ}だと{思|おも}われていたが、のちに{大|おお}きな{功績|こうせき}を{残|のこ}した。
examples.english: He was considered an insignificant person, but later left behind great achievements.

notes:
A literary expression meaning "not worth taking up" or "not worth considering." Has an elevated, slightly formal tone and is commonly encountered in writing, speeches, and formal conversation.

COMMON PATTERNS:
Composed of {取|と}る (to take) + に (particle) + {足|た}らない (not sufficient). The underlying meaning is "not sufficient to be taken up [for discussion/attention]."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {取|と}るに{足|た}らない{問題|もんだい}: a trivial problem
- {取|と}るに{足|た}らない{話|はなし}: a trivial matter
- {取|と}るに{足|た}らない{存在|そんざい}: an insignificant existence
- {取|と}るに{足|た}らない{人物|じんぶつ}: an insignificant person

SIMILAR WORDS:
- くだらない: worthless; stupid — more colloquial and dismissive, often expressing contempt. {取|と}るに{足|た}らない is more measured and literary.
- たいしたことない: no big deal — casual and reassuring. {取|と}るに{足|た}らない is more formal and definitive.
- つまらない: boring; trivial — broader in meaning; can mean "boring" or "worthless." {取|と}るに{足|た}らない specifically means "not worth considering."
